title: Friend of victim apologizes at Roha fatality inquiry
article: One of the last people to see Tamer Sayed Roha alive apologized to his friend's family Friday, saying he was too stoned on cocaine to help the 27-year-old Calgary man.
Alexander Jay spoke frankly at a fatality inquiry into the death of Roha, who died of cocaine-induced excitation delirium in 2002, saying his friend was "tripping out really bad."
"I just want to give my deepest apologies to Tamer's family for not trying to help out, but at the time I wasn't really in a position to help," said Jay.
Jay is the final witness in the inquiry that was called after Roha died in police custody when officers attended his room at the Quality Inn at 2359 Banff Trail N.W.
After his death, Roha's family accused police of harming their son. A report is expected in late May.
Jay said Roha called him repeatedly the day he died, Sept. 4, 2002, wanting him to come to the hotel.
"He was moving really fast, talking really fast.
"He was distraught and thought people were outside," he said.
"I wasn't worried because his behaviour was always odd and I was really high and getting sketched out."
Earlier in the inquiry, court heard from hotel employees who described Roha as being sweat-drenched and saying and doing odd things.
Roha stopped breathing shortly after police handcuffed him and was declared dead at Foothills Hospital.
Toxicology reports showed he had high levels of cocaine in his system.
Roha's family was aware of their son's drug problems and had made several failed attempts to make him get help.
They were representing themselves at the inquiry.
